screening_results.reason: This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–55) using the Attention Network Test. It includes an explicitly reported within-subject executive-control contrast (incongruent > congruent), and reports group-level second-level voxelwise results with coordinates (within-sample task effects and genotype group comparisons). Participant demographics, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are all described. Although ROI masks were defined for hypothesis testing, the manuscript reports voxelwise activation coordinates from the within-group (whole-sample) task analysis, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level task-evoked results. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, resting baseline only, non-empirical, or out-of-range participants) are met. Full text appears complete with background, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an fMRI study using an n-back working memory task (executive function) in healthy adult participants (mean age 23.3). Analyses include within-subject contrasts (e.g., Clever vs Stupid primes; error vs correct trials) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical mapping (conjunction analyses corrected for multiple comparisons and exploratory whole-brain searches; coordinates and SPM results reported). Task paradigm, imaging modality, participant demographics, and methods are fully described. The study therefore meets all required inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI with whole-brain group results and reports coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; within healthy 18–60 sample; active control conditions used). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of executive function (cognitive set shifting) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and adequate reporting of participants, modality, and paradigm, the paper uses fixation/rest as the baseline for within-participant contrasts and does not employ an active control condition. This violates inclusion criterion I6 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation as the only baseline). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I6. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (SST variant) in healthy adults that reports within-subject contrasts and group-level whole-brain analyses (FWE-corrected). However, the full text does not report participant ages nor an explicit statement confirming the sample as healthy (methods list 'Fourteen right handed participants' but no ages or explicit health status). Inclusion criterion I10 requires reporting of participant age and confirmation of healthy sample status; this information is missing, so not all inclusion criteria are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered: whole-brain results are reported and this is not a connectivity-only, between-group, rest-baseline-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range-age study based on available text. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded because I10 is not satisfied.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive function (inhibition, attentional shifting, response initiation). It includes within-participant contrasts (e.g., stop–go, shift–go, stop–shift, double–stop) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected statistics and peak coordinates. Participant information (healthy adults aged 18–40), imaging modality (3T fMRI), and detailed task paradigms are provided. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is complete. Excluded because the study includes participants outside the target healthy adult range and is not restricted to healthy individuals (E8). Although the study uses PET and a within-participant contrast versus an active control and reports whole-brain voxelwise results, the task (visual navigation) is not within the specified executive function domains required by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (within-participant contrast vs active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described), I10 (participant information, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (study does not assess a canonical executive function/cognitive control task), I9 (task does not fall within listed executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore excluded based on E8.

Although the study administered executive function tasks and reports participant demographics and PET modality, it does not provide task-evoked, within-participant whole-brain activation contrasts. PET data were resting FDG measures acquired prior to behavioral testing and correlations with behavior; no task-based PET/fMRI activation maps or within-subject task vs active-control contrasts are reported. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI/PET assessing executive function), I6 (within-participant task vs active control contrast), I7 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), and I8 (clear whole-brain task results). Included criteria met: I9 (tasks are within executive domains) and I10 (participant ages, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigms are reported). Exclusion criteria triggered: E4 (resting-state/task-less imaging without task activation maps) and E8 (study sample not restricted to healthy individuals; includes remitted MDD subjects). Conclusion: Exclude.

This study reports a task-based fMRI investigation of sustained attention (vigilance, an executive function domain) including a healthy adult control group (ages 18–50). It contains within-participant contrasts against an active control (visual countdown baseline) and event-related contrasts (correct rejections vs. other trial types). The paper describes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (composite within-group activation maps with voxelwise one-sample t-tests and cluster correction), and reports whole-brain results in text/figures and ROI analyses. Participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are all reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of executive control (stop-signal task) in healthy adults (ages 22–42). It reports within-subject contrasts (stop vs go; post-stop stop-success vs post-go stop-success), uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses in SPM with reported coordinates and thresholding, and provides participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task details. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting-baseline only, participants are healthy and within 18–60). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back), an established executive function. It reports within-subject contrasts (one- and two-back vs zero-back active control), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps using permutation-based cluster inference. Participant details (healthy adults aged 21–29), imaging modality (3T BOLD fMRI), and task paradigm are all clearly reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (stop-signal task), an executive function domain (inhibition). It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., StopSuccess vs StopFailure; StopSuccess vs Go with 0% stop probability) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-level inference and reported coordinates/figures. Participant information (n=24, ages 19–26, healthy) and imaging modality (3T fMRI) and detailed task paradigm are provided. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, baseline includes active Go trials, and sample is healthy adults within 18–60. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This fMRI paper investigates amygdala responses to anticipation of pain while subjects perform a Continuous Performance Task (CPT) as an active coping manipulation. Although imaging, healthy adult sample, ages, and task details are reported (I10), the study does not meet the meta-analysis requirements: (1) the primary focus is emotional/pain anticipation rather than an executive-function/cognitive-control task contrast (fails I5 and I9); (2) it does not provide a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation map for an executive-function contrast — results are reported as ROI-based amygdala analyses (meets exclusion E3 and fails I7/I8); and (3) there is no within-participant contrast of an executive function task versus an active control condition as required (fails I6). Therefore the study should be excluded from a meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This study reports task-based BOLD fMRI in healthy adults performing an N-Back working memory task (executive function). It includes within-subject contrasts (2-Back vs 0-Back active control), group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise results and reported coordinates (with correction and small-volume results), and provides participant demographics and imaging/task details. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not patient-group-only, participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This empirical study used task-based fMRI in healthy adults performing the Conners' Continuous Performance Test (a vigilance/inhibition executive task). The authors report within-subject contrasts (task blocks vs baseline/active control of meaningless images) and group-level voxelwise analyses (one-way ANOVA producing whole-brain t-maps and cluster-level activations). Participant age, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, baseline is active images rather than fixation-only, empirical data in healthy 18–60 y/o). Although sample size is small (n=8), this does not conflict with the stated inclusion/exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an fMRI investigation of working memory manipulation (executive function domain) in healthy adults and reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked maps. However, the published fMRI contrasts are reported versus a fixation (rest) baseline: 'multisubject statistical maps for all tasks (color, angle, and dual) compared with fixation'. The meta-analysis requires at least one within-participant contrast of an executive task relative to an active control condition (I6). Because the whole-brain reported maps use fixation as the baseline (a passive baseline) and no clearly described whole-brain task-versus-active-control contrast is provided, the study violates exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I6. Exclusion criterion met: E6. Therefore exclude.

This is an fMRI study of passive viewing of violent, fearful, and neutral film clips in healthy adults. Although it reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (satisfying I7) and provides participant, health-status, and imaging details (satisfying I10), it does NOT assess an executive function or cognitive-control task (fails I5 and I9). The paradigm is passive viewing rather than an executive-domain task (e.g., inhibition, working memory, cognitive flexibility), and therefore there is no within-participant contrast of an executive function task vs an active control condition as required (fails I6). No exclusion criteria are specifically triggered. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Inclusion criteria met: I7, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6, I9. Exclusion criteria met: none.

Excluded for E8: participants fall partly outside the target adult age range (reported ages 16–21, including minors <18), violating the review’s 18–60 years restriction. Study otherwise meets the methodological inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI working memory), I6 (within-subject contrasts vs. 0-back active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-thresholding and reported coordinates), I8 (whole-brain results reported with MNI coordinates), I9 (working memory = established executive function domain), and I10 (reports participant ages, healthy status screening, imaging modality, and task paradigm). No other exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of inhibitory control (antisaccade) with whole-brain voxelwise group analyses and reported coordinates, it includes participants younger than 18 (adolescents 13–17) alongside adults and is not restricted to an 18–60-year-old healthy adult sample. This violates exclusion criterion E8 for the meta-analysis focused on healthy adults only. Additionally, the reported contrasts focus on reward vs neutral conditions within the antisaccade task and task epochs vs fixation baseline; the manuscript does not provide a within-participant contrast of the executive function (inhibition) task relative to an active non-inhibitory control condition required by inclusion criterion I6. Therefore, despite meeting I5, I7, I8, I9, and I10, the study must be excluded from this adult-focused meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI task study of cognitive control/executive function (temporal integration, working memory, strategy maintenance) in healthy adults (n=26, mean age 22.4). It reports within-subject contrasts between task conditions (W2 vs W12) and state/item decompositions, and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (cluster tables/coordinates, maps versus fixation and between-condition contrasts). Participant health status, age, imaging modality, and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory and visual search in healthy adults (ages 19–32). It reports within-participant contrasts including dual-task vs an active control (‘Visual search only’) and other task contrasts, uses group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses with voxelwise statistical maps and reports coordinates/tables, and provides detailed participant, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI) and task-paradigm information. The tasks fall within an executive function domain (working memory). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, out-of-range or unhealthy samples) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This study is an fMRI/NIRS investigation of spatial working memory with whole-brain, voxelwise analyses and reports coordinates; it includes healthy adult control within-group results and provides participant and task details. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI of executive function - working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain maps), I8 (coordinates and figures reported), I9 (task is working memory, an executive function), I10 (participant, modality and task information reported). However, the study does not include an active control condition contrast; the task-related analyses use fixation/ITI or correct vs error trials and contrasts appear to be task vs baseline (fixation) or within-task performance contrasts rather than an executive task vs an active control task. The review exclusion criterion E6 (rest or fixation as the only baseline condition without an active control task) is therefore met. Inclusion criterion I6 (within-participant contrast of task relative to an active control) is not met. Because E6 is met and I6 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function (working memory load and distractor interference). It reports within-participant contrasts (incongruent vs congruent; load × congruency interactions) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with thresholds and cluster results. Tasks fall within executive domains (working memory, inhibition/response control). Participant demographics (healthy adults aged 18–35), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly reported. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, resting-state baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range/clinical samples) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be included.

This study reports original task-based fMRI data in healthy young adults (median age 22, range 18–25) using an n-back working memory task (executive function). The authors performed within-subject contrasts (two-back vs active ‘x-target’ baseline) and second-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with reported cluster coordinates and thresholds. Task paradigm, participant health status, age range, and imaging modality are clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task activations, uses an active baseline, empirical fMRI data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is a within-subject task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=23, mean age 21.3) probing selective/object-based attention and top-down cognitive control. It reports within-participant contrasts (attend vs ignore/observe) using active control conditions, and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunctions and state contrasts) with thresholding described. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. The selective attention task targets cognitive control/top-down biasing processes and thus falls within executive/cognitive-control domains relevant to the review. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, uses active control conditions, healthy adult sample). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the study includes participants outside the target population for the meta-analysis: it includes a patient group (Turner syndrome) rather than being restricted to healthy adults, and includes participants younger than 18 (age range for Turner group includes 14-year-old), thus violating exclusion criterion E8. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function — working memory tasks), I6 (within-participant contrasts across task conditions/domains and distracter vs no-distracter), I9 (tasks fall within executive function domain — working memory), I10 (participant ages, health status of control group, imaging modality and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no clear report of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical map in the main text; results are primarily ROI-based with group-average activation maps reported in supplementary figures but no clearly described voxelwise group-level statistical maps for inclusion). Because E8 is met, the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults aged 18–60.

This fMRI study uses a task that elicits cognitive interference (semantic–prosodic conflict) analogous to Stroop-like executive control tasks, and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses contrasting incongruent (CONF) vs congruent (NOCONF) conditions. Participants are healthy adults (ages 24–38). Imaging modality (fMRI), task paradigm, behavioral results, and whole-brain statistical results are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive function activations and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults (ages 18–28). It reports within-subject contrasts between binding conditions and an active single-item non-binding baseline, conducts group-level, whole-brain (second-level voxelwise) analyses (with FDR correction), and presents whole-brain results in figures/tables. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults explicitly comparing deceptive (lie) vs truthful responses and false vs true recognition. Deception contrasts (Lie vs Truth) constitute within-subject executive/cognitive-control task contrasts, analyzed at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise random-effects statistics and reported coordinates/thresholds. Participants are healthy adults (n=20, age range 19–28). Imaging modality, task paradigm, and participant health/age are all reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI task study of working memory with emotional distraction in healthy adults (female, 18–33). It uses a within-subject task contrast (emotional vs. neutral vs. scrambled distracters), reports group-level random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunctions, maps, figures, and ROI follow-ups), and provides participant demographics and imaging protocol. The working memory task falls within executive function. Thus all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (Sternberg task) in healthy adults (mean age 24.8). It includes within-subject contrasts (e.g., ss5>ss2), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses (SPM5) with coordinate tables and figures, and provides participant, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task details. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are met. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

Although the study meets the methodological inclusion criteria (fMRI task-based executive paradigms, within-participant task vs active control contrasts, whole-brain voxelwise group analyses with coordinates reported, tasks within executive-function domains, and adequate participant/age/imaging/task information), it includes a clinical sample (participants with Autism Spectrum Disorder) alongside healthy controls. This means the study sample is not restricted to healthy individuals, which violates exclusion criterion E8. Therefore the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis limited to healthy adults. Inclusion IDs met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion IDs not met: none. Exclusion IDs met: E8 (study includes non-healthy participants).

This study used fMRI in healthy adult samples and analyzed task data (including 3-back working memory) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps, and reports results clearly — satisfying I5, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the presented analyses focus on trial-by-trial RT regressors and task-vs-fixation contrasts (fixation baseline), and I find no within-participant contrast of an executive function task relative to an active control condition (e.g., 3-back vs 0-back or another active control). Therefore I6 is not met. Because the study appears to use fixation/rest as the baseline for task-related contrasts without reporting an active control contrast, exclusion criterion E6 applies. Conclusion: EXCLUDED for failing to meet I6 (and triggering E6).

Although this fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level, within-subject contrasts and provides participant demographics and imaging details, it does not examine a task that falls within the review's specified executive function domains. Met: I5 (fMRI task-based study addressing cognitive control/conflict), I6 (within-participant contrasts: Magic vs Causal Control; Surprise vs Causal Control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (results reported as coordinates/tables and described), I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, modality, and task paradigm reported). Not met: I9 — the paradigm involves perception of magic tricks and violations of causal expectation (a perceptual/reasoning paradigm probing disbelief/conflict detection) rather than established executive function tasks (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The authors interpret activations in terms of conflict/cognitive-control, but the task was not designed or categorized as a canonical executive function task. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) were triggered. Therefore the study is excluded for failing I9.

Although this study is a task-based fMRI investigation of sustained attention (vigilance) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses in a healthy control sample, it does not include an active control condition for the required within-participant task vs active-control contrast. The task contrasts are reported primarily against a fixation baseline and practice (novel vs. practice) repetitions; therefore the study uses rest/fixation as the primary baseline rather than an active control. This violates exclusion criterion E6 and fails inclusion criterion I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive domain—vigilance), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analyses), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables), I9 (task falls within executive function domain—vigilance), and I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-subject contrast against an active control).

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of working memory (N-back), an executive function task, in healthy adults. It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., 2-back/4 vs 2-back/1 and conditions vs 0-back), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FDR correction, and presents whole-brain activation maps and cluster results in text/figures. Participant demographics (mean age 26.6, healthy screened) and imaging modality (3T BOLD fMRI) and task paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, inappropriate sample age/health) are met. Full article content (background, methods, results, discussion) is present, so fulltext is complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (age 19–33) examining working memory manipulation (an executive function). It includes within-subject contrasts (manipulation cue vs retrieval cue) and other within-participant contrasts. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cue minus maintenance contrast reported at p<0.05 FDR and shown in figures) and provides coordinates and descriptions of results. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a task-based fMRI study of an executive function (2-Back verbal working memory) (I5, I9); it includes within-participant contrasts of the executive task vs an active control (2-Back vs 0-Back) (I6); group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical analyses are reported (one-sample t-tests, thresholding, and group summary maps) and results/ROIs are derived from these maps (I7, I8); and the paper reports participant ages, confirms a screened healthy sample (healthy right-handed smokers without current psychiatric/neurological disorders), specifies the imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigm (I10). The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, resting-only baseline, non-empirical, or unhealthy/out-of-range participants) are met. Therefore the study is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This fMRI study of olfactory delayed-match-to-sample working memory in healthy adults meets multiple inclusion criteria (I5: task-based fMRI; I6: within-subject contrasts between task conditions; I9: working memory is an established executive function domain; I10: participant ages, healthy status, imaging modality and task paradigm are reported). However, the manuscript reports ROI-based analyses (piriform subdivisions, inferior frontal gyrus) and uses a conservative ROI approach and functional localizers; it does not present group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps, whole-brain coordinate tables, or equivalent whole-brain results in the text or supplements. Therefore it fails I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Consequently, the study is excluded.

This is an fMRI study of working-memory (n-back) in healthy adults that reports participant details, imaging modality, and task paradigm (meets I5, I9, I10). However, the primary analyses are tensor-ICA (resting-state/functional connectivity) focusing on the default mode network timecourse and component maps. The paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map (e.g., standard GLM contrasts such as 2-back>0-back) or equivalent task activation maps; results are connectivity/component-based and timecourse statistics. Therefore it fails to provide the required whole-brain task activation map and is excluded under E4 (connectivity/resting-state analyses without whole-brain task activation). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (within-participant contrast of executive task vs active control for a task-evoked activation) and I7 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked map). Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI investigation of auditory and visual spatial working memory in healthy adults (ages 22–39) and reports group-level, surface-based whole-brain statistical maps; it therefore meets I5, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the experimental contrasts focus on delay-period activity relative to baseline/fixation (and similar rest/fixation comparisons) rather than an executive-task contrasted against an active control condition. No within-participant contrast against an active control condition (I6) is reported. Because the study uses fixation/rest as the baseline without an active control task, it violates exclusion criterion E6. Therefore it must be excluded.

EXCLUDED because the paper reports only region-of-interest/multivariate decoding analyses (V1–V4 ROI-based pattern classification) and does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or coordinate/figure-based whole-brain results. This meets exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI examining working memory, an executive function), I9 (task falls within an executive function domain — working memory), and I10 (reports participant ages, healthy sample, imaging modality, and task paradigm). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no clear within-participant contrast of an executive task versus an active control reported as a standard task activation contrast), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map), and I8 (no acceptable reporting of whole-brain results in coordinates/figures). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded under E3.

This fMRI study examines working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults and reports whole-brain voxelwise results, but its control condition is passive visual fixation (subjects instructed to fixate a crosshair). Inclusion criterion I6 requires a within-participant contrast versus an active control, and exclusion criterion E6 bars studies using rest/fixation as the only baseline. Therefore the study must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function/working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis reported via SPM and thresholding), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables/figures), I9 (task falls within executive function domains—working memory), I10 (participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no active control; only fixation baseline). Exclusion criterion met: E6 (rest/fixation-only baseline). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an original, task-based fMRI study of working memory manipulation (executive function) in healthy adults (mean age 25, n=18). It reports within-participant contrasts (color vs angle; conjunction vs color/angle) using a group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM with voxelwise inference and cluster-size thresholding; coordinates and statistical thresholds are provided. Imaging modality (3T fMRI), participant health/age, and task paradigm details are fully reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function) in healthy adults (mean age 27.4) that reports group-level, whole-brain task analyses and coordinates. The experiment includes within-participant contrasts of experimental (working memory) tasks versus active control tasks, and task PLS produced whole-brain activation patterns (with local maxima/coordinates) suitable for meta-analysis. Connectivity analyses are also present but do not replace the whole-brain task activation results. All required participant, imaging modality, and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups only, includes active control, empirical, and participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an fMRI, whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analysis in healthy adult participants and reports coordinates. It includes a within-subject contrast (semantic categorization > passive listening). However, the task is a semantic language categorization task, not an established executive function domain (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I5 (study assessing executive function/cognitive control) and I9 (task within established executive function domains), and consequently I6 (contrast of an executive function task vs active control) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that directly probes short-term/working memory (an executive function domain) using a pitch memory task. The study reports within-participant contrasts (pitch memory > active motor control) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99) with coordinates, thresholds, and cluster results. Participant age (18–40), healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task activations, uses an active control). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria listed below.
